description: Commands that create a `.strictmetadata` directory's `manifest.toml` while writing a record (`rlsbl release backfill`, `rlsbl release abandon`) now commit the manifest with the record instead of leaving it uncommitted
A refusing command prints no partial report: `rlsbl status` refusing a member with several targets and no `--target` no longer prints an empty status block before the error

New `rlsbl transition public-client --subject <name> --reason <text>` declares that a subject of a confidential repository has a public client, taking its registry names and the repository's names out of the confidential-name index; `transition show` lists the declarations, and the index no longer holds releasable names or identity values, nor matches a name inside a URL or a dotted hostname
`transition show` holds the confidential-names rule for a confidential repository whose public-client declarations leave it no name to protect, expecting no index entry, instead of calling it public
After a three-way merge conflict is resolved, the next `rlsbl scaffold` commits the resolved file and its new merge base, which it used to leave uncommitted.

**rlsbl is rewritten in Go.** One `rlsbl` binary replaces the Python package. It is distributed as the Go module `github.com/stricttools/rlsbl`, as npm packages under the existing `rlsbl` name (the binary in one package per platform, `rlsbl-linux-x64`, `rlsbl-linux-arm64`, `rlsbl-darwin-x64`, and `rlsbl-darwin-arm64`, selected through `optionalDependencies`), and as PyPI wheels under the existing `rlsbl` name. There are no Windows packages, and rlsbl's Python modules can no longer be imported.

**rlsbl's records move to `.strictmetadata/`.** rlsbl reads nothing of the old layout (`.rlsbl/`, `.rlsbl-monorepo/`, and each member's `.rlsbl/`). Run `rlsbl migrate records` once in every repository, with `--dry-run` first: it converts the declarations, changelogs, release files and archives, batch release files, transition record, scaffold state, hook scripts, and options entries, writes the lifecycle-and-license record (`--licenses` states a license the manifests do not), removes the old layout through saferm, and commits. `rlsbl monorepo cleanup` removes old-layout residue, in a standalone repository too.

**One declarations file.** `config.json`, `workspace.toml`, and `releasable.toml` are replaced by `.strictmetadata/releasables/releasables.toml`, declaring the layout, release branches, releasables, members, targets, pipelines, hooks, and checks; its `[timeouts]` table (`push_seconds`, `ci_seconds`, `check_seconds`, `hook_seconds`) replaces the `push_timeout`, `ci_timeout`, `check_timeout`, and `hook_timeout` keys, and behavior switches are options entries in `.strictmetadata/options/`, written with `rlsbl options set`. `rlsbl migrate records` writes both.
**The release targets are go, npm, and pypi.** The `spec` target is removed, and `rlsbl migrate records` refuses a configuration naming any target other than go, npm, and pypi, naming the hand edit.

**Changelog format version 2.** Each releasable's changelog lives in `.strictmetadata/changelog/<releasable>/`, every entry carries an id, and an entry naming more commits than the per-entry limit carries its reason through `rlsbl changelog add --batch-reason`, which replaces `--allow-batch` and the `batch_limits` exclusions; `rlsbl migrate records` restamps existing entries.

**The pre-release channel is removed.** Versions are `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`: a release file carrying `preid`, `blog`, or `bump = "prerelease"` is refused, and `rlsbl migrate records` folds a pre-release's changelog entries into the stable version it preceded.

**Removed subsystems.** Member layering (the `[layers]` key and the layers-violations check), deploy configuration (a server releasable declares a `deploy_command` instead), subtree mirror publication, the launcher artifact, local asset upload (`assets` and `custom_assets`; the publish workflow builds and attaches release archives in CI), the Cloudflare Pages pipeline (selfdoc deploys documentation sites), blog-on-release, and the `requires-services` (with the `services` and `test_env` keys), `private-hook-stale`, and `mixed-tag-schemes` checks are removed.

**Removed commands and flags.** `rlsbl deploy`, `rlsbl prs`, `rlsbl pre-push-check`, `rlsbl monorepo mirror`, `rlsbl monorepo snapshot`, `rlsbl monorepo snapshot-check` (`rlsbl monorepo graph --json` gives the same inventory on demand), `rlsbl transition record`, `rlsbl release undo --target`, and `rlsbl changelog amend --id` are removed.

**Source checks move to strictcode.** The lint, format, and type-check tool options, the dependency-declaration checks, and the dead-modules, circular-deps, library-lint, dead-workspace-packages, ruff-lint, and strictspec certificate checks leave rlsbl; the `rlsbl:strictcode` option (error by default) runs `strictcode analyze` as a release check and refuses a missing strictcode, and `rlsbl migrate records` moves their settings into `strictcode.toml`.

**The lifecycle-and-license record.** Each repository's `.strictmetadata/lifecycle-and-license/lifecycle-and-license.toml` holds each releasable's dated lifecycle, license, and identities. A release or resume of a releasable on hold or retired is refused; a proprietary releasable requires a private repository and refuses every public output (registry packages, attestations, the Go module proxy, public docs); a Go library target on a private repository is refused; and `rlsbl monorepo init`, `rlsbl monorepo add`, and `rlsbl monorepo absorb` creating a releasable require `--license`.

**Changed flags.** `rlsbl release reconcile` takes `--mode plan` or `--mode apply` instead of `--plan` and `--apply`; `rlsbl monorepo release init` requires `--releasables` or `--all`, writing no table for every releasable unasked; and `rlsbl monorepo graph` requires `--format`.

**Preflight checks always run.** A declared `pre_release` hook replaces only a member's built-in tests, never the preflight checks, and customized hook scripts become hooks declared in `releasables.toml`, moved by `rlsbl migrate records` to `.strictmetadata/release-hooks/`.
A release refuses an origin remote whose host is a domain other than github.com; SSH host aliases without a dot are accepted.

**New `rlsbl transition` commands** keep the lifecycle-and-license record: `transition show` prints the record with every rule's verdict, `transition lifecycle`, `transition license`, `transition identity`, and `transition unversioned-tag` record periods and tags, `transition classify` makes a releasable proprietary, `transition declassify` squashes the proprietary history and takes a repository public, and `transition init-minimal-record` writes a minimal record into a repository rlsbl does not manage.

**Confidential names stay out of public output.** The `confidential-names` check refuses a tracked file or changelog entry of a public repository carrying a name from the machine-local confidential-name index, every GitHub Release body rlsbl writes is scanned the same way, and every mutating command keeps the index in step with the lifecycle-and-license record.
A release refuses a packed artifact (an npm tarball, a wheel, or a Go module zip) carrying a file from outside the releasable's members, naming each file.

`rlsbl monorepo graph --json` prints the dependency graph as a document: the members in topological order with their versions, targets, releasables, flags, dependencies, and dependents, and the edges in the same order.
**npm ships Go binaries.** A go binary pipeline publishes to npm as one package per platform, selected through the main package's `optionalDependencies` by `os` and `cpu`, with no postinstall script.
`rlsbl rewrite project-name` records each renamed identity in the lifecycle-and-license record as a pending identity, one per registry carrying the name, which takes effect with the next release.
`rlsbl release deprecate` and `rlsbl release yank` accept the latest release, which they used to refuse in favor of `rlsbl release undo`.
`rlsbl scaffold` refuses to write a new `VERSION` that would disagree with a target's version.

the commits of the Go rewrite's foundation slice: the module, the test harness, git, saferm, and GitHub plumbing, the application, the declarations, and the workspace model, with their decision records

the commits of the Go rewrite's records slice: the release record, the transition record, run state, targets, pipelines, publishing rules, options, and the changelog model, with their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's scaffold slice: templates, workflows, routers, the CI wait, dependency readers, and the rewrite commands, with their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's command slice: watch, release notes, upstream, dev, secrets, options, status, unreleased, targets, and commit, with their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's checks slice: the checks framework and the project, changelog, prepush, release, lifecycle, external, and strictcode checks, with their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's monorepo, past-release, and history-rewrite slices, with their remaining checks and decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's changelog, transition, release-validation, extract, and absorb slices, with their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's documentation and record-migration slices, with the fixes found while making the suite compile, and their decision records
the commits of the Go rewrite's release-steps and batch-release slices and its help-text finishing fixes, with their decision records
the commits fixing the findings of the Go rewrite's blind audit, with their decision records
the commits carrying out the orchestrator rulings, the selfdoc pass, and the record migration of the Go rewrite's release campaign, with their decision records

description: The `npm-token-synced` check runs inside `rlsbl check`, `rlsbl failing-checks`, and a release's `--dry-run`; it failed there because listing the npm tokens was not an allowed read.

A go binary pipeline whose main package is not at the module root gets a `.goreleaser.yml` and archives named after that package (`./cmd/tool` builds `tool`), not after the module path's last element; and `rlsbl scaffold` keeps the `version.go` it wrote into the main package instead of removing it on the next run and writing it again on the one after.

`rlsbl scaffold` writes a stub `go.mod` into the `.strictmetadata/` of a Go module below the repository root when that module tracks files there (the strictcli schema dump), so the module zip leaves them out and the `upload-private-paths` check's fix clears it.
The `npm-token-synced` check reads npm 10's token listing, where a revoked token carries its revocation time; it reported that `npm token list --json` printed no list of tokens.

A release file whose `exclude` names a target a pipeline publishes is refused, naming the pipeline: every pipeline publishes on every release, so the excluded target was published anyway. Delete the pipeline from `releasables.toml` to release without publishing that target.

A release no longer fails in the release checkout of a repository whose working tree holds an uncommitted `go.work`: every program the release starts, the strictcli schema dump's entry-point detection, the preflight checks, and the packed-artifact listing included, gets the release's `GOWORK` (the checkout's own committed `go.work`, or off), so Go never picks up the working tree's `go.work` from the checkout below it.

The PyPI binary wheels a pypi go-binary pipeline publishes carry the project's readme as their description, with its content type, and its keywords and classifiers, so the PyPI project page shows the readme; a readme whose suffix names no content type, or a readme table without one, is refused.
